summary: Light-ion femtoscopy and efficient collider ML provide the strongest contributions. Other relevant work develops a charm-response scaling benchmark and a photon-TMD inversion for ultraperipheral collisions, both with important evidential limitations. A baryon-stopping transport extraction is flagged for overstrong interpretation.
professional_summary: The selected papers emphasize nuclear-geometry sensitivity in azimuthal femtoscopy, empirical charm-versus-light anisotropy response, conditional inversion of coherent photon distributions, and resource-efficient Lorentz-aware collider learning.
strongest_paper: 2610.29760: azimuthal femtoscopy as a high-sensitivity discriminator of ab initio O-16 and Ne-20 geometry; 2610.29439: systematic distillation of efficient Lorentz-aware jet taggers.
strongest_paper_summary: The femtoscopy study offers the clearest new heavy-ion observable, while the jet-distillation study has the strongest validation and immediate computational relevance.

papers.title: Nuclear Geometry-Driven Femtoscopic Correlations in Light-Ion Collisions
papers.short_authors: Dániel Kincses, Bithika Karmakar, Iurii Karpenko, Boris Tomášik
papers.abstract: A hybrid calculation combining ab initio oxygen and neon configurations, TRENTo initial conditions, viscous hydrodynamics, and UrQMD predicts substantially enhanced azimuthal femtoscopic eccentricity ratios for deformed nuclei. The Ne+Ne/O+O freeze-out-eccentricity ratio reaches about 1.5–1.8 in central events and remains stable when pre-equilibrium free streaming is removed.
papers.critical_assessment: Strong. The calculation is high-statistics, uses two independent ab initio configuration sets and a spherical control, and tests one important model variation. Remaining risk is model dependence beyond the tested free-streaming switch, including bulk-parameter calibration and final-state interaction treatment.

papers.title: Heavy-Quark Dynamics from D0-Meson Anisotropy-Response Scaling Violations
papers.abstract: Published D0-meson v2 and v3 measurements in Pb+Pb, p+Pb, and Au+Au are transformed relative to a light-meson response reference. A charm-specific attenuation factor is introduced to restore the common scaling, with reported system- and centrality-dependent values.
papers.critical_assessment: Mixed. The cross-system synthesis is interesting, but the paper does not present a conventional global fit, goodness-of-fit measure, or transparent propagated uncertainty on the extracted scaling parameters; some light- and charm-hadron inputs also use nonidentical centrality intervals. Treat the numerical k_c values as an empirical parametrization, not a transport-coefficient determination.

papers.title: Direct Access to Nuclear Photon TMDs with In Situ Probes in Ultraperipheral Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.abstract: The paper proposes extracting a nuclear photon occupation number from a ratio of radiative lepton-pair cross sections in ultraperipheral collisions. Under scalar statistical factorization, the occupation factor multiplies a complete tree-level reference, while finite bins and detector migration turn the inversion into a weighted average.
papers.critical_assessment: Interesting but not yet demonstrated. The extraction depends on scalar factorization, neglects finite-size Coulomb corrections at the present order, and supplies no realistic rate or detector study. The author states these limitations; experimental usefulness remains an open feasibility question.

papers.title: How Far Can Foundation Models Be Distilled for Efficient Jet Tagging?
papers.short_authors: Jay Agarwal, Siddharth Khare, Dhruv Kumar
papers.abstract: Six teachers spanning architectures, symmetries, and pretraining are distilled into five compact students on a top-tagging benchmark. A 20k-parameter L-GATr-slim student exceeds published from-scratch taggers in the authors’ comparison, while a 2k-parameter model matches ParT; code, weights, and hardware-oriented cost measurements are released.
papers.critical_assessment: Strong within its benchmark. The controlled teacher–student matrix, three-run uncertainties, inference measurements, and released artifacts are real strengths. External validity is still limited by a single simulated binary top-tagging dataset and one distillation setup; detector/domain-shift robustness is not established.

papers.title: Lorentz-Equivariant Geometric Algebra Transformers for Top-Quark Event Reconstruction
papers.short_authors: E. Abasov, L. Dudko, A. Markina, M. Perfilov, P. Volkov, G. Vorotnikov, A. Zaborenko
papers.abstract: Lorentz-equivariant geometric-algebra transformers are evaluated on tW/ttbar discrimination, FCNC classification, and universal event reconstruction. They outperform or match transformer baselines on parts of the program, but a handcrafted high-level MLP remains best for the FCNC task.
papers.critical_assessment: Promising but mixed. Breadth and released implementation are positives, and the authors report three-seed variation for the FCNC comparison. Gains are task-dependent, some comparisons use different information content, and the study does not yet establish robustness to detector mismodeling or real data.

cautions.title: Multi-Energy Analysis of Baryon Stopping: Extracting Non-Equilibrium Dynamics via Stochastic Rapidity Diffusion
cautions.abstract: A blast-wave interpolation of net-proton spectra is combined with an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck-style rapidity diffusion model to infer friction, diffusion, relaxation, and a longitudinal Reynolds number over a wide beam-energy range. The paper reports a roughly 163-fold fall in that Reynolds number.
cautions.critical_assessment: Caution. Several downstream uncertainties are assigned as fixed percentages, the momentum-diffusion input carries an assumed 20% error, and the derived Reynolds number depends on the chosen blast-wave and linear-drift construction. Claims that a diffusion-dominated regime is 'completely reached' and that higher-energy data would only inflate uncertainty are substantially stronger than the demonstrated evidence.
